questions.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y}^{2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/79326f0f463d3b26db4ab497045fa35aa5aa7fb68be6fd79b5ebd633a4d6646f.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y\le x\le 2\}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x,
$$

and the bottom boundary is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. Its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le x\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/4452d48cac6bd387e8f7f27a9aedfbe51f9c5e478a5288f889aa3378c4805d34.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y}^{2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}[y]_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-{e}^{-4}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/472aa6b0afe20f7c1902446102265f758637c9ec00eb985bf38a658dc92f3fe5.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le {x}^{3}\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2-x\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y={x}^{3}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt[3]{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=2-x\,⟹\,x=2-y.
$$

To change the order of integration we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\sqrt[3]{y}\le x\le 2-y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/77b59ce5c40514338b0d23a31e7028c7fa0f7343aad018576301fcc4ec441ac1.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{2-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{8}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/d5d777577f85cd577ce35bfd3a99c1e2218622d1856f4fe7ee4afe1cfd2c9f86.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 8,\,\sqrt[3]{y}\le x\le 2\}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=\sqrt[3]{y}\,⟹\,y={x}^{3},
$$

and the bottom boundary is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. Its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le {x}^{3}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/05ec37a8f4fd33c05a2438df5c5fbc697f8b560fde0b9fe73922a0db56a09c2c.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{8}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}[{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}[y]_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}\,{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}{e}^{{x}^{4}}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({e}^{16}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}-1}^{1-{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/abf9e5dda9e98caac491aa5d94b3e2ae3f08f90d6bd490762adabc1437ac49d9.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{3}-1\le y\le 1-{x}^{2}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/a45e4b63b1eff23617abcbe33ce522652b20de6c817dfde2d9cdda52d12bb778.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{y+1}.$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$\,$ $x=\sqrt{1-y}.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{y+1}\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-y}\}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}-1}^{1-{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{y+1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}-1}^{-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/926e4c717707d13fdb9562e149d2f41c3ab657b42fbae35c0953019ab93a06b6.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-{y}^{2}-1\le x\le -y\}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226206/assets/8933233e8aca4a36ee90ffec69ca6e93d0523d3fa50c400d2cdea78f9ec80812.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $y=y(x),$  are 

$\,$ $y=\sqrt{-x-1}\,$ and $\,y=1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=-x.$ 

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le -1,\,\sqrt{-x-1}\le y\le 1\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,0\le y\le -x\}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}-1}^{-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{\sqrt{-x-1}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
